In this notebook, we translate the R code for Chapter 2 of Peng Ding's open-access textbook [Linear Model and Extensions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00649) to PyFixest. The book's R scripts and data sets are on the Harvard Dataverse ([doi:10.7910/DVN/DBDYVJ](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/DBDYVJ), CC0 1.0). Other chapters are tracked in [this GitHub issue](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/957).

```{python}
import pandas as pd

import pyfixest as pf
```

## Chapter 2: OLS with a Univariate Covariate

Chapter 2 fits a line through Galton's data on the heights of parents and their adult children: 934 children from 205 families. `midparentHeight` is the average of the father's height and 1.08 times the mother's height, and `childHeight` is the child's height, both in inches.

```{python}
# read the data from the Harvard Dataverse. The server rejects the default
# user agent of Python's urllib, so we set our own.
dataverse = "https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/access/datafile/"
storage_options = {"User-Agent": "pyfixest-docs"}

# file GaltonFamilies.txt, the data set the book's chapter02.R reads
galton = pd.read_csv(dataverse + "10123762", sep=r"\s+", storage_options=storage_options)
galton.head()
```
